newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India churns, Pakistan firmer.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India churns, Pakistan firmer.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) churned, with some more activity ahead of the market's closure for the Diwali festival on Friday, while Pakistan was better bid after the ouster of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto.
"Tomorrow is the last real trading day before the festival, today was a real "churn and burn' day on the Indian market, which was under pressure," said a trader.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed down 0.83 points, or 1.35 percent, at 60.10 points, with the premium over the local market at 12.58 percent compared with yesterday's 12.80 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index fell 29.88 points, or 0.97 percent to 3,062.84.

There was demand for Bajaj Auto, off 58 cents at $32.00/$33.50, BSES, off 17 cents at $18.50/$19.50, Grasim, up 20 cents at $13.00/$14.00 and good two way business in Ashok Leyland, off 94 cents at $10.25/$11.25, the trader said.
ITC continued under pressure, with the GDRs down 39 cents at $7.75/$8.75 after last week's allegation company officials had violated India's Foreign Exchange Regulation Act.
On Tuesday, major shareholders said they would review operations of ITC at a board meeting on November 15.
Among Pakistan counters, where the market was closed for a holiday, traders saw good demand after the sacking overnight of Bhutto by President Farooq Leghari.
"The local market will open up five percent tomorrow," a trader forecast.
Pakistan Telecom was trading at $82.50/$84.50 and Hubco at $23.25/23.50.

"The fundamentals are still there. It is good that they have got rid of some of the corruption and scandal but the future depends on what the International Monetary Fund and World Bank think," said the trader.
Meraj Khalid, a veteran politician, will head a caretaker cabinet and has promised elections for February 3.

Elsewhere in Asia, the Capel Korea GDR Index ended little changed, off just 0.03 points at 64.94, a premium of 29.07 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index fell 13.74 points, or 1.84 percent, to a provisional close of 733.68.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended down 0.20 points at 89.84, a premium of 1.26 percent after the Taiwan Weighted Index ended 18.47 points or 0.28 percent lower at 6,604.14.
